featured.name: GestureOS
featured.pitch: Control a Windows PC with your bare hands through a webcam.
highlights: Turns hand tracking (21 landmarks per hand) into mouse, scroll, media, drawing and app-launch control.
Starts disarmed. A two-palm hold arms it, and one gateway releases held keys when it disarms.
630 automated tests drive the real engine with generated hands and a fake input backend, so it is tested without a camera.

featured.name: Life-RPG Protocol
featured.pitch: A gamified productivity app where focus sessions and peer-reviewed proof of work earn XP.
highlights: Audited my own database and found users could edit their own Aura, XP and role.
Fixed it with column-level grants, a revoked function right, and identity taken from auth.uid().
44 attack checks failed on the old schema; about 260 database checks pass now, including a two-session race test.

featured.name: Browser Arcade
featured.pitch: Two multiplayer board games, Shadow Hunt and Game of Trades, playable on one screen or online.
highlights: Found that 26 of 26 state snapshots exposed the hidden player's position, then fixed it with per-seat views and host validation.
A test reads every message sent to every non-hidden seat across a whole online game.
135 tests run on every push with GitHub Actions.

featured.name: Textile Defect ML Model
featured.pitch: A leak-aware study of how much your data split changes a fabric-defect detector's results.
highlights: On the public AITEX dataset (245 strips, 7 fabrics), a random split overstated random-forest patch-level average precision by 0.44 against splitting by strip.
With a whole fabric held out, every method scored close to chance.
Intervals come from 1,000 bootstrap resamples over strips; 75 tests pass.

about: I'm a third-year B.Tech Computer Science and Engineering student at Ahmedabad University.
